+++ b/src/server/maintenance/restore-cold-custody.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,294 @@
+import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
+import { existsSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
+import {
+  chmod,
+  link,
+  lstat,
+  mkdir,
+  mkdtemp,
+  readFile,
+  realpath,
+  rename,
+  rm,
+  symlink,
+  writeFile,
+} from 'node:fs/promises';
+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
+import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
+import { afterEach, expect, test, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { restoreBarrierPath } from './restore-barrier.ts';
+import {
+  activatePreparedRestoreOriginal,
+  captureColdRestoreCustody,
+  captureRestoreOriginals,
+  coldRestoreCustodyInputs,
+  commitRestoreFiles,
+  preserveColdRestoreCustody,
+  preserveRestoreOriginals,
+  stagePreparedRestoreOriginal,
+  validColdRestoreCustody,
+} from './restore-files.ts';
+import type {
+  ColdRestoreCustodyOptions,
+  RestoreFileControl,
+  RestoreFilePhase,
+} from './restore-files.ts';
+
+const directories: string[] = [];
+afterEach(async () => {
+  for (const directory of directories.splice(0))
+    await rm(directory, { recursive: true, force: true });
+});
+const evidence = (bytes: Uint8Array) => ({
+  bytes: bytes.length,
+  sha256: createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex'),
+});
+async function fixture() {
+  const directory = await realpath(await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'spinel-cold-custody-')));
+  directories.push(directory);
+  const root = join(directory, 'recovery'),
+    databasePath = join(directory, 'live.sqlite'),
+    prepared = join(directory, 'prepared.sqlite');
+  await mkdir(root, { mode: 0o700 });
+  const original = Buffer.alloc(160_003, 0x41),
+    interrupted = Buffer.alloc(131_079, 0x42),
+    replacement = Buffer.alloc(70_001, 0x43),
+    wal = Buffer.from('interrupted private trial WAL');
+  await writeFile(databasePath, original, { mode: 0o600 });
+  const id = randomUUID(),
+    assertClosed = vi.fn();
+  const originals = await preserveRestoreOriginals({ root, databasePath, id, assertClosed });
+  // Custody must handle an interrupted overwrite without assuming valid SQLite.
+  await writeFile(databasePath, interrupted);
+  await writeFile(databasePath + '-wal', wal, { mode: 0o600 });
+  await writeFile(databasePath + '-shm', '', { mode: 0o600 });
+  await writeFile(prepared, replacement, { mode: 0o600 });
+  const marker = restoreBarrierPath(databasePath);
+  await writeFile(
+    marker,
+    JSON.stringify({ version: 1, operationId: id, identity: originals.identity }) + '\n',
+    { mode: 0o600 },
+  );
+  const options: ColdRestoreCustodyOptions = {
+    root,
+    databasePath,
+    id,
+    captureId: randomUUID(),
+    identity: originals.identity,
+    deadline: Date.now() + 60_000,
+    assertClosed,
+  };
+  const phases: RestoreFilePhase[] = [];
+  const control: RestoreFileControl = {
+    root,
+    databasePath,
+    deadline: options.deadline,
+    assertClosed,
+    readPhase: () => phases.at(-1),
+    async persist(phase) {
+      phases.push(phase);
+    },
+  };
+  const job = join(root, `restore-${id}`),
+    capture = join(job, `cold-${options.captureId}`),
+    raw = join(capture, 'raw');
+  return {
+    root,
+    databasePath,
+    original,
+    interrupted,
+    replacement,
+    wal,
+    prepared,
+    originals,
+    marker,
+    options,
+    control,
+    phases,
+    job,
+    capture,
+    raw,
+    files: { ...originals, candidate: evidence(replacement) },
+  };
+}
+
+test('cold custody retains a partial closed tuple without claiming a logical witness or changing original custody', async () => {
+  const f = await fixture(),
+    manifest = await captureColdRestoreCustody(f.options);
+  expect(existsSync(f.capture)).toBe(false);
+  expect(validColdRestoreCustody(manifest)).toBe(true);
+  expect(manifest.files['spinel.sqlite']).toEqual(evidence(f.interrupted));
+  expect(manifest).not.toHaveProperty('witness');
+  expect(manifest).not.toHaveProperty('fingerprint');
+  await preserveColdRestoreCustody(f.options, manifest);
+  const saved = join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite'),
+    inode = (await lstat(saved)).ino;
+  expect(await readFile(saved)).toEqual(f.interrupted);
+  expect(await readFile(join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite-wal'))).toEqual(f.wal);
+  expect(await readFile(join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite-shm'))).toHaveLength(0);
+  expect(coldRestoreCustodyInputs(f.root, manifest)).toEqual({
+    database: { path: saved, ...evidence(f.interrupted) },
+    wal: { path: join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite-wal'), ...evidence(f.wal) },
+  });
+  await expect(preserveColdRestoreCustody(f.options, manifest)).resolves.toEqual(manifest);
+  expect((await lstat(saved)).ino).toBe(inode);
+  expect(await readFile(join(f.job, 'original', 'spinel.sqlite'))).toEqual(f.original);
+  expect(await readFile(f.databasePath)).toEqual(f.interrupted);
+  // The ordinary original-capture path must still refuse a restore barrier.
+  await expect(captureRestoreOriginals(f.options)).rejects.toThrow('unfinished');
+});
+
+test.each([
+  'missing-barrier',
+  'wrong-barrier',
+  'wrong-identity',
+  'open-owner',
+  'expired',
+  'journal',
+  'public-directory',
+  'symlink',
+  'hardlink',
+])('cold capture refuses %s before creating custody', async (kind) => {
+  const f = await fixture();
+  if (kind === 'missing-barrier') await rm(f.marker);
+  if (kind === 'wrong-barrier')
+    await writeFile(
+      f.marker,
+      JSON.stringify({ version: 1, operationId: randomUUID(), identity: f.originals.identity }),
+    );
+  if (kind === 'wrong-identity') f.options.identity = { device: '1', inode: '2' };
+  if (kind === 'open-owner')
+    f.options.assertClosed = () => {
+      throw new Error('Workspace owner is still open.');
+    };
+  if (kind === 'expired') f.options.deadline = Date.now() - 1;
+  if (kind === 'journal') await writeFile(f.databasePath + '-journal', '', { mode: 0o600 });
+  if (kind === 'public-directory') await chmod(dirname(f.databasePath), 0o755);
+  if (kind === 'symlink') {
+    await rename(f.databasePath + '-wal', f.databasePath + '-other');
+    await symlink(f.databasePath + '-other', f.databasePath + '-wal');
+  }
+  if (kind === 'hardlink') await link(f.databasePath, f.databasePath + '-alias');
+  await expect(captureColdRestoreCustody(f.options)).rejects.toThrow();
+  expect(existsSync(f.capture)).toBe(false);
+});
+
+test('partial activation can retain original live modes inside its private directory', async () => {
+  const f = await fixture();
+  for (const suffix of ['', '-wal', '-shm']) await chmod(f.databasePath + suffix, 0o644);
+  const manifest = await captureColdRestoreCustody(f.options);
+  await preserveColdRestoreCustody(f.options, manifest);
+  for (const name of ['spinel.sqlite', 'spinel.sqlite-wal', 'spinel.sqlite-shm']) {
+    expect((await lstat(join(f.raw, name))).mode & 0o077).toBe(0);
+    expect(await readFile(join(f.raw, name))).toEqual(
+      await readFile(f.databasePath + name.slice('spinel.sqlite'.length)),
+    );
+  }
+});
+
+test.each(['changed-wal', 'missing-wal', 'new-sidecar', 'changed-manifest'])(
+  'a persisted cold capture cannot be redefined after %s',
+  async (kind) => {
+    const f = await fixture();
+    if (kind === 'new-sidecar') await rm(f.databasePath + '-shm');
+    const manifest = await captureColdRestoreCustody(f.options);
+    if (kind === 'changed-wal') await writeFile(f.databasePath + '-wal', 'different');
+    if (kind === 'missing-wal') await rm(f.databasePath + '-wal');
+    if (kind === 'new-sidecar') await writeFile(f.databasePath + '-shm', '', { mode: 0o600 });
+    if (kind === 'changed-manifest') manifest.captureId = randomUUID();
+    await expect(preserveColdRestoreCustody(f.options, manifest)).rejects.toThrow();
+    expect(existsSync(f.capture)).toBe(false);
+  },
+);
+
+test('a cancelled cold copy preserves partial bytes and refuses an overwrite retry', async () => {
+  const f = await fixture();
+  await chmod(f.databasePath, 0o644);
+  const manifest = await captureColdRestoreCustody(f.options),
+    abort = new AbortController(),
+    target = join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite');
+  f.options.signal = abort.signal;
+  f.options.assertAuthorized = () => {
+    if (existsSync(target) && statSync(target).size >= 64 * 1024) abort.abort();
+  };
+  await expect(preserveColdRestoreCustody(f.options, manifest)).rejects.toThrow();
+  expect((await lstat(target)).size).toBe(64 * 1024);
+  f.options.signal = undefined;
+  f.options.assertAuthorized = undefined;
+  await expect(preserveColdRestoreCustody(f.options, manifest)).rejects.toThrow();
+  expect((await lstat(target)).size).toBe(64 * 1024);
+  expect(await readFile(f.databasePath)).toEqual(f.interrupted);
+});
+
+test('cold original activation uses the shared installer and preserves both raw generations', async () => {
+  const f = await fixture(),
+    manifest = await captureColdRestoreCustody(f.options),
+    attempt = randomUUID(),
+    inode = (await lstat(f.databasePath)).ino;

+# SPN-128 — recover a preserved original after interruption
+
+## Scope checkpoint
+
+2026-11-01, accepted for implementation by agent judgment under the standing
+persona delegation. The complete L outcome includes a supported cold-host
+command, separately journaled authority and crash cuts, immutable source proof,
+existing rollback reconciliation and original trial admission, terminal replay
+protection, real-process acceptance, and the maintained recovery runbook.
+SPN-124's operation lifetime and SPN-125's pruning remain separate.
+
+## Fresh cold-host authority and immutable restore history
+
+2026-11-01, accepted by agent judgment under the standing persona delegation.
+The question is how an Operator authorizes recovery when the interrupted
+restore's application proof has expired. Renewing that proof would change the
+meaning of the immutable intent; requiring a fresh application login would be
+impossible while the workspace is closed. The existing private host control
+socket supplies deliberate authority without either dependency.
+
+The existing private, service-UID-owned control socket is the Operator's
+cold-host authority when application sign-in is unavailable. A deliberate
+`recover-original --operation UUID` command obtains a new bounded grant for the
+exact unresolved job. It never refreshes the old passkey proof or rewrites its
+intent. The original phase/execution and each interrupted recovery attempt stay
+available as historical evidence. Missing or contradictory evidence keeps the
+workspace closed.
+
+Each grant uses the existing two-minute supervisor budget, with a hard ten-minute
+upper bound for configured test budgets. Each job retains at most eight cold
+attempts and still obeys the existing 64 KiB record bound; exhausted capacity
+refuses another attempt without deleting any evidence.
+These limits keep the command finite and the retained journal inspectable.
+Increasing operation lifetime and safely pruning retained evidence remain the
+separate SPN-124 and SPN-125 outcomes.
+
+Recovery uses the witnessed frozen original as the only content/access source
+and `reconcileRestoreRollback` for the existing access, receipt and generation
+reconciliation. Every known complete attempted image contributes negative
+evidence. A partially overwritten live database is retained as raw evidence and
+never opened as SQLite. An interrupted private trial must still match its sealed
+prepared fingerprint before its closed tuple can supply negative evidence.
+
+The existing `original` permit, private readiness and durable commitment protocol
+opens the result. A committed winner is immutable: retry/restart can finish
+opening that current generation but cannot reinstall old bytes over subsequent
+acknowledged work.
+
+A trial permit is journaled before the main journal adopts its child. A crash
+between those writes can leave a private process outside the main child field.
+Fresh host authority may stop only the exact selected planned group after
+checking the predecessor generation and operation authority, then the process
+boot, start time and ownership token. Recovery checks unchanged evidence and
+physical handle closure before granting a new attempt; other live groups still
+keep the workspace closed.
+
+Operator: a supported bounded command replaces manual fresh-host recovery.
+Owner and Collaborator: preserve work accepted after the most recent backup,
+including history, filing and access, with the established reconciliation fences.
+Link guest: old capability access is revoked as in ordinary original recovery.
+
+## What the fingerprint proves
+
+The frozen source's full logical fingerprint must match the independently
+persisted pre-shutdown witness. Reconciliation intentionally changes sessions,
+native generations, negative receipt evidence and the recovered notice. Therefore
+the final live fingerprint matches the newly prepared recovered output; original
+user content and access are checked separately. No fingerprint fields are
+excluded or weakened to force equality.
+
+## Verification
+
+The acceptance harness uses actual SIGKILL and restart at eleven historical
+restore cuts and six cold-command cuts. Fixture-only clocks expire the original
+proof and previous cold grants; this is clock-controlled expiry, not a wall-clock
+soak. Checks bind the source to its shutdown witness and the live result to the
+reconciled output before fresh authentication, verify revoked sessions and guest
+links, and preserve an acknowledged Owner edit and passkey counter across another
+restart and repeated command. Missing or altered originals and a changed private
+trial fingerprint must refuse without changing the live tuple or barrier.
+Exact executed source, check and review identities, measurements, and failure
+dispositions are maintained in [PR 229](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/229).
+Final CI and independent reviews must identify the same current committed source;
+this description of the harness does not claim those gates have already passed.
+
+## Required-validation prerequisites
+
+2026-11-01, accepted by agent judgment under the standing persona delegation.
+The first full acceptance run on `f3bdf95e1355de5bebf8ee64332b31201555b9c5`
+passed the 626-test recovery partition, including all 17 process crash cases,
+the 123 supervisor tests and both supervised-restore browser journeys. It also
+exposed two bounded preparation gaps in unchanged validation infrastructure:
+the Ubuntu mirror optimizer rejected an AWS runner profile before tests started,
+and the shared-folder offline-creation journey failed its first attempt before
+publication. Its automatic retry passed; `failOnFlakyTests` correctly kept the
+required gate failed. That retry is not evidence of repair.
+
+The maintained [browser first-attempt record](evidence/SPN-128-sync-production-first-attempt.json)
+retains the exact source, runtime, browser, original artifact digest, timeout,
+retry and observed state without credentials or document contents. Its seven-day
+raw CI artifact is supplementary and expires. The first attempt has no retained
+trace establishing its exact blocked action; its missing-folder screen and
+absence of forwarded creation are consistent with the source-supported
+preparation race, not proof of that historical interleaving.
+The [mirror setup record](evidence/SPN-128-mirror-setup-failure.json) retains both
+failed jobs. Neither printed its mirror file. Synthetic test profiles are not
+claimed to reproduce those exact missing contents; final CI must demonstrate
+the actual candidate's setup and workloads.
+
+Under [the runbook's verification-gap rule](../run-backlog.md#4-fix-here-or-file-separately)
+and the recorded [SPN-117 prerequisite](SPN-117.md), this PR may carry only the
+minimum proven preparation fixes needed to obtain its required acceptance:
+wait for the requested empty folder's loaded contents before disconnecting, and
+leave a non-Azure mirror profile unchanged by the Azure-specific optimization.
+The estimate is fewer than 100 changed executable lines, including extracting
+the existing mirror transform for focused tests, plus regression evidence and
+this decision record. Final actual counts belong in the PR.
+Neither fix changes application behavior, test assertions, timeouts, retries,
+runner selection or required gates. Strict validation remains before any Azure
+mirror rewrite; apt installation and its failures remain visible.
+
+Before changing folder readiness, the bounded sequence is three controlled
+fresh-profile held-folder probes, then three complete corrected first-attempt
+journeys, then one withheld-readiness negative case. No unchanged retries are
+authorized by this plan. The existing heading and New button may render from
+the shared list before the separate folder-detail response supplies the loaded
+view. The contents signal establishes synchronous view readiness; later offline
+reloads and publication assertions still prove persistence. If the probe instead
+finds an application persistence defect, reassess its ownership before expanding
+this slice. Preserve the original failure, diagnostic patches and each result.
+
+The [bounded readiness record](evidence/SPN-128-readiness.json) retains all
+seven attempts and the reproducible
+[held-folder](evidence/SPN-128-held-folder-probe.patch),
+[four-line repair](evidence/SPN-128-readiness-fix.patch) and
+[withheld-readiness](evidence/SPN-128-withheld-readiness.patch) patches.
+All three held-response probes reproduced heading/New visibility with loading
+still active, no contents and no prepared folder view; disconnecting then
+produced the missing view. All three complete corrected journeys passed their
+first attempts with the original content, access, reload, receipt and exactly-once
+publication assertions intact. The single negative case actually failed at the
+existing 5,000 ms Folder contents assertion before disconnecting or creating a
+document. Its exit 1 is negative-control evidence, not a passing journey.
+
+Each attempt used a fresh isolated browser context, fixture database and account,
+one worker and zero retries; it does not claim separate Chromium process restarts.
+Node 26.12.1, Playwright 1.64.1 and Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (revision 1248) were
+pinned. The serialized host-accounted watchdog reported 34.80 seconds/1,708.8 MiB
+for the three probes, 81.88 seconds/2,031.9 MiB for the three corrected journeys,
+and 45.17 seconds/1,692.1 MiB for the negative command, within its unchanged
+2 GiB/475-second bounds. Exact source, configuration, diagnostic and artifact
+hashes and the difference between assertion, suite and watchdog elapsed times
+are retained in the JSON. Only the four-line readiness repair runs in the
+committed fixture; diagnostic patches are evidence. These controlled results
+establish the preparation gap without claiming the historical timeout's exact
+interleaving or completing SPN-120's broader audit.
+
+Exercise mirror applicability with a non-Azure profile left byte-identical, the
+ordinary and already-preferred Azure pairs, and malformed Azure profiles that
+must still fail before writing. Record the actual runner-profile evidence and
+its limits rather than guessing its contents from the provider name.
+
+The [focused mirror checks](evidence/SPN-128-mirror-validation.json) passed all
+12 cases on pinned Node 26.12.1: synthetic profiles without the Azure hostname
+remain byte-identical, recognized priorities and surrounding bytes are preserved,
+and nine malformed Azure cases refuse. The serialized host-accounted watchdog
+reported 1.0 second and 105.3 MiB peak, within its 2 GiB/475-second bounds. The
+helper does not validate or rewrite profiles without that hostname; downstream
+apt and test steps still run normally. The original failed profiles remain
+unknown, and these local cases do not replace the actual final-head CI run.
+
+The prerequisite's actual executable diff is four added fixture lines, 39 added
+and 26 removed mirror-helper lines, and 48 new focused-test lines: 117 changed
+lines including tests. Most helper changes extract the existing strict transform
+for direct testing. This accounting excludes maintained evidence and prose;
+the final PR records the complete base-relative size.
+
+Operator receives required checks that reach their existing workloads and stop
+at an unfinished preparation phase. Owner and Collaborator retain the complete
+offline content, ownership, reload, access and exactly-once publication contract.
+Link guest gains no capability; its access and revocation checks stay required.
+This prerequisite claims no completion of SPN-120's historical fixture audit or
+broader cleanup work. Only SPN-128 is prepared for retirement by this PR; opening
+it does not authorize merging it.

-
-# 🌷 SPN-128 Reinstall the preserved original after an interrupted restore
-
-## Story
-
-As the [Owner](../product/personas.md#owner), I want a restore interrupted during its trial to reopen on the workspace's own preserved content, so that a power loss or timeout does not cost work saved after the last backup.
-
-## Scenarios
-
-### The host stops during the candidate's trial
-
-Given a confirmed restore that preserved the original and activated the candidate, then lost power or ran past its confirmation window before committing,
-When the supervisor restarts and the Operator follows the unresolved-restore runbook,
-Then a supported supervisor command verifies the preserved original against its frozen fingerprint and reinstalls it as a new generation,
-And the restore records **Original content was recovered**, with the recovered banner and the same access reconciliation as an in-flight rollback,
-And ambiguous or missing evidence still keeps the workspace closed.
-
-## Rules
-
-- Split by SPN-112's merge review, 2026-10-30: [disposition](../implementation/SPN-112.md#merge-review-dispositions). SPN-112 fails and reopens a restore that stopped before activation, stays fail-closed from activation onward, and documents fresh-host recovery from the last backup in `docs/maintenance.md`, which loses work after that backup.
-- The command is supervisor-owned and journaled with its own crash cuts, needs fresh Operator authority, and never copies raw files over a live or newly acknowledged generation. Reuse `reconcileRestoreRollback` and the original-recovery permit rather than a second rollback path.
-- Pre-launch: the launch drill (SPN-038) exercises restore on the target host, where an interruption today means lost work.
-- Persona weighing: the Owner and Collaborators keep their latest work; the Operator gets a supported exit instead of fresh-host recovery; Link guests are revoked either way.
-
-## Out of scope
-
-- Lifting the five-minute window (SPN-124); evidence pruning (SPN-125).
-
-## Verify
-
-- Real-process SIGKILL tests at trial-opening, activation, original-activation and original-commit, each followed by restart, the new command, and a check that the live fingerprint equals the frozen original's.
-- Runbook step in `docs/maintenance.md` replaced by the supported command.

@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import { preferUbuntuArchive } from './prefer-ubuntu-archive.ts';
+
+const azure = 'http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const archive = 'https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const security = 'https://security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const normal = `${azure}\tpriority:1\n${archive}\tpriority:2\n${security}\tpriority:3\n`;
+const preferred = `${azure}\tpriority:2\n${archive}\tpriority:1\n${security}\tpriority:3\n`;
+
+test('leaves profiles without Azure byte-identical', () => {
+  // Synthetic non-Azure inputs, not a claimed capture of a particular runner.
+  for (const original of [
+    '',
+    `${archive}\tpriority:1\n${security}\tpriority:2\n`,
+    '# runner-managed sources\r\nhttp://us-east-1.ec2.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/\tpriority:1\r\n',
+    'http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/\n',
+  ]) {
+    assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(original), original);
+  }
+});
+
+test('changes only the existing Azure/archive priorities and preserves other bytes', () => {
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(normal), preferred);
+  const original = `# mirrors\r\n  ${azure}\tpriority:1  \r\n\t${archive} priority:2\r\n${security}\tpriority:3\r\n`;
+  const expected = `# mirrors\r\n  ${azure}\tpriority:2  \r\n\t${archive} priority:1\r\n${security}\tpriority:3\r\n`;
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(original), expected);
+});
+
+test('keeps an already preferred Azure/archive pair unchanged', () => {
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(preferred), preferred);
+});
+
+for (const [name, original] of [
+  ['missing archive', `${azure}\tpriority:1\n`],
+  ['duplicate Azure', normal + `${azure}\tpriority:1\n`],
+  ['duplicate archive', normal + `${archive}\tpriority:2\n`],
+  ['equal priorities', normal.replace(`${archive}\tpriority:2`, `${archive}\tpriority:1`)],
+  ['unsupported priority', normal.replace(`${azure}\tpriority:1`, `${azure}\tpriority:3`)],
+  ['missing priority', normal.replace(`${azure}\tpriority:1`, azure)],
+  ['unexpected metadata', normal.replace('priority:1', 'priority:1 extra:yes')],
+  ['unrecognized Azure scheme', normal.replace(azure, azure.replace('http:', 'https:'))],
+  ['unrecognized Azure case', normal.replace('azure.archive', 'AZURE.archive')],
+]) {
+  test(`refuses malformed Azure profile: ${name}`, () => {
+    assert.throws(() => preferUbuntuArchive(original), /expected one Azure\/archive pair/);
+  });
+}

index 0000000..a4e579f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/server/maintenance/restore-cold-custody.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,294 @@
+import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
+import { existsSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
+import {
+  chmod,
+  link,
+  lstat,
+  mkdir,
+  mkdtemp,
+  readFile,
+  realpath,
+  rename,
+  rm,
+  symlink,
+  writeFile,
+} from 'node:fs/promises';
+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
+import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
+import { afterEach, expect, test, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { restoreBarrierPath } from './restore-barrier.ts';
+import {
+  activatePreparedRestoreOriginal,
+  captureColdRestoreCustody,
+  captureRestoreOriginals,
+  coldRestoreCustodyInputs,
+  commitRestoreFiles,
+  preserveColdRestoreCustody,
+  preserveRestoreOriginals,
+  stagePreparedRestoreOriginal,
+  validColdRestoreCustody,
+} from './restore-files.ts';
+import type {
+  ColdRestoreCustodyOptions,
+  RestoreFileControl,
+  RestoreFilePhase,
+} from './restore-files.ts';
+
+const directories: string[] = [];
+afterEach(async () => {
+  for (const directory of directories.splice(0))
+    await rm(directory, { recursive: true, force: true });
+});
+const evidence = (bytes: Uint8Array) => ({
+  bytes: bytes.length,
+  sha256: createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex'),
+});
+async function fixture() {
+  const directory = await realpath(await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'spinel-cold-custody-')));
+  directories.push(directory);
+  const root = join(directory, 'recovery'),
+    databasePath = join(directory, 'live.sqlite'),
+    prepared = join(directory, 'prepared.sqlite');
+  await mkdir(root, { mode: 0o700 });
+  const original = Buffer.alloc(160_003, 0x41),
+    interrupted = Buffer.alloc(131_079, 0x42),
+    replacement = Buffer.alloc(70_001, 0x43),
+    wal = Buffer.from('interrupted private trial WAL');
+  await writeFile(databasePath, original, { mode: 0o600 });
+  const id = randomUUID(),
+    assertClosed = vi.fn();
+  const originals = await preserveRestoreOriginals({ root, databasePath, id, assertClosed });
+  // Custody must handle an interrupted overwrite without assuming valid SQLite.
+  await writeFile(databasePath, interrupted);
+  await writeFile(databasePath + '-wal', wal, { mode: 0o600 });
+  await writeFile(databasePath + '-shm', '', { mode: 0o600 });
+  await writeFile(prepared, replacement, { mode: 0o600 });
+  const marker = restoreBarrierPath(databasePath);
+  await writeFile(
+    marker,
+    JSON.stringify({ version: 1, operationId: id, identity: originals.identity }) + '\n',
+    { mode: 0o600 },
+  );
+  const options: ColdRestoreCustodyOptions = {
+    root,
+    databasePath,
+    id,
+    captureId: randomUUID(),
+    identity: originals.identity,
+    deadline: Date.now() + 60_000,
+    assertClosed,
+  };
+  const phases: RestoreFilePhase[] = [];
+  const control: RestoreFileControl = {
+    root,
+    databasePath,
+    deadline: options.deadline,
+    assertClosed,
+    readPhase: () => phases.at(-1),
+    async persist(phase) {
+      phases.push(phase);
+    },
+  };
+  const job = join(root, `restore-${id}`),
+    capture = join(job, `cold-${options.captureId}`),
+    raw = join(capture, 'raw');
+  return {
+    root,
+    databasePath,
+    original,
+    interrupted,
+    replacement,
+    wal,
+    prepared,
+    originals,
+    marker,
+    options,
+    control,
+    phases,
+    job,
+    capture,
+    raw,
+    files: { ...originals, candidate: evidence(replacement) },
+  };
+}
+
+test('cold custody retains a partial closed tuple without claiming a logical witness or changing original custody', async () => {
+  const f = await fixture(),
+    manifest = await captureColdRestoreCustody(f.options);
+  expect(existsSync(f.capture)).toBe(false);
+  expect(validColdRestoreCustody(manifest)).toBe(true);
+  expect(manifest.files['spinel.sqlite']).toEqual(evidence(f.interrupted));
+  expect(manifest).not.toHaveProperty('witness');
+  expect(manifest).not.toHaveProperty('fingerprint');
+  await preserveColdRestoreCustody(f.options, manifest);
+  const saved = join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite'),
+    inode = (await lstat(saved)).ino;
+  expect(await readFile(saved)).toEqual(f.interrupted);
+  expect(await readFile(join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite-wal'))).toEqual(f.wal);
+  expect(await readFile(join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite-shm'))).toHaveLength(0);
+  expect(coldRestoreCustodyInputs(f.root, manifest)).toEqual({
+    database: { path: saved, ...evidence(f.interrupted) },
+    wal: { path: join(f.raw, 'spinel.sqlite-wal'), ...evidence(f.wal) },
+  });
+  await expect(preserveColdRestoreCustody(f.options, manifest)).resolves.toEqual(manifest);
+  expect((await lstat(saved)).ino).toBe(inode);
+  expect(await readFile(join(f.job, 'original', 'spinel.sqlite'))).toEqual(f.original);
+  expect(await readFile(f.databasePath)).toEqual(f.interrupted);
+  // The ordinary original-capture path must still refuse a restore barrier.
+  await expect(captureRestoreOriginals(f.options)).rejects.toThrow('unfinished');
+});
+
+test.each([
+  'missing-barrier',
+  'wrong-barrier',
+  'wrong-identity',
+  'open-owner',
+  'expired',
+  'journal',
+  'public-directory',
+  'symlink',
+  'hardlink',
+])('cold capture refuses %s before creating custody', async (kind) => {
+  const f = await fixture();
+  if (kind === 'missing-barrier') await rm(f.marker);
+  if (kind === 'wrong-barrier')
+    await writeFile(
+      f.marker,
+      JSON.stringify({ version: 1, operationId: randomUUID(), identity: f.originals.identity }),
+    );
+  if (kind === 'wrong-identity') f.options.identity = { device: '1', inode: '2' };
+  if (kind === 'open-owner')
+    f.options.assertClosed = () => {
+      throw new Error('Workspace owner is still open.');
+    };
+  if (kind === 'expired') f.options.deadline = Date.now() - 1;
+  if (kind === 'journal') await writeFile(f.databasePath + '-journal', '', { mode: 0o600 });
+  if (kind === 'public-directory') await chmod(dirname(f.databasePath), 0o755);
+  if (kind === 'symlink') {
+    await rename(f.databasePath + '-wal', f.databasePath + '-other');
+    await symlink(f.databasePath + '-other', f.databasePath + '-wal');

+# SPN-128 — recover a preserved original after interruption
+
+## Scope checkpoint
+
+2026-11-01, accepted for implementation by agent judgment under the standing
+persona delegation. The complete L outcome includes a supported cold-host
+command, separately journaled authority and crash cuts, immutable source proof,
+existing rollback reconciliation and original trial admission, terminal replay
+protection, real-process acceptance, and the maintained recovery runbook.
+SPN-124's operation lifetime and SPN-125's pruning remain separate.
+
+## Fresh cold-host authority and immutable restore history
+
+2026-11-01, accepted by agent judgment under the standing persona delegation.
+The question is how an Operator authorizes recovery when the interrupted
+restore's application proof has expired. Renewing that proof would change the
+meaning of the immutable intent; requiring a fresh application login would be
+impossible while the workspace is closed. The existing private host control
+socket supplies deliberate authority without either dependency.
+
+The existing private, service-UID-owned control socket is the Operator's
+cold-host authority when application sign-in is unavailable. A deliberate
+`recover-original --operation UUID` command obtains a new bounded grant for the
+exact unresolved job. It never refreshes the old passkey proof or rewrites its
+intent. The original phase/execution and each interrupted recovery attempt stay
+available as historical evidence. Missing or contradictory evidence keeps the
+workspace closed.
+
+Each grant uses the existing two-minute supervisor budget, with a hard ten-minute
+upper bound for configured test budgets. Each job retains at most eight cold
+attempts and still obeys the existing 64 KiB record bound; exhausted capacity
+refuses another attempt without deleting any evidence.
+These limits keep the command finite and the retained journal inspectable.
+Increasing operation lifetime and safely pruning retained evidence remain the
+separate SPN-124 and SPN-125 outcomes.
+
+Recovery uses the witnessed frozen original as the only content/access source
+and `reconcileRestoreRollback` for the existing access, receipt and generation
+reconciliation. Every known complete attempted image contributes negative
+evidence. A partially overwritten live database is retained as raw evidence and
+never opened as SQLite. An interrupted private trial must still match its sealed
+prepared fingerprint before its closed tuple can supply negative evidence.
+
+The existing `original` permit, private readiness and durable commitment protocol
+opens the result. A committed winner is immutable: retry/restart can finish
+opening that current generation but cannot reinstall old bytes over subsequent
+acknowledged work.
+
+A trial permit is journaled before the main journal adopts its child. A crash
+between those writes can leave a private process outside the main child field.
+Fresh host authority may stop only the exact selected planned group after
+checking the predecessor generation and operation authority, then the process
+boot, start time and ownership token. Recovery checks unchanged evidence and
+physical handle closure before granting a new attempt; other live groups still
+keep the workspace closed.
+
+Operator: a supported bounded command replaces manual fresh-host recovery.
+Owner and Collaborator: preserve work accepted after the most recent backup,
+including history, filing and access, with the established reconciliation fences.
+Link guest: old capability access is revoked as in ordinary original recovery.
+
+## What the fingerprint proves
+
+The frozen source's full logical fingerprint must match the independently
+persisted pre-shutdown witness. Reconciliation intentionally changes sessions,
+native generations, negative receipt evidence and the recovered notice. Therefore
+the final live fingerprint matches the newly prepared recovered output; original
+user content and access are checked separately. No fingerprint fields are
+excluded or weakened to force equality.
+
+## Verification
+
+The acceptance harness uses actual SIGKILL and restart at eleven historical
+restore cuts and six cold-command cuts. Fixture-only clocks expire the original
+proof and previous cold grants; this is clock-controlled expiry, not a wall-clock
+soak. Checks bind the source to its shutdown witness and the live result to the
+reconciled output before fresh authentication, verify revoked sessions and guest
+links, and preserve an acknowledged Owner edit and passkey counter across another
+restart and repeated command. Missing or altered originals and a changed private
+trial fingerprint must refuse without changing the live tuple or barrier.
+Exact executed source, check and review identities, measurements, and failure
+dispositions are maintained in [PR 229](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/229).
+Final CI and independent reviews must identify the same current committed source;
+this description of the harness does not claim those gates have already passed.
+
+## Required-validation prerequisites
+
+2026-11-01, accepted by agent judgment under the standing persona delegation.
+The first full acceptance run on `f3bdf95e1355de5bebf8ee64332b31201555b9c5`
+passed the 626-test recovery partition, including all 17 process crash cases,
+the 123 supervisor tests and both supervised-restore browser journeys. It also
+exposed two bounded preparation gaps in unchanged validation infrastructure:
+the Ubuntu mirror optimizer rejected an AWS runner profile before tests started,
+and the shared-folder offline-creation journey failed its first attempt before
+publication. Its automatic retry passed; `failOnFlakyTests` correctly kept the
+required gate failed. That retry is not evidence of repair.
+
+The maintained [browser first-attempt record](evidence/SPN-128-sync-production-first-attempt.json)
+retains the exact source, runtime, browser, original artifact digest, timeout,
+retry and observed state without credentials or document contents. Its seven-day
+raw CI artifact is supplementary and expires. The first attempt has no retained
+trace establishing its exact blocked action; its missing-folder screen and
+absence of forwarded creation are consistent with the source-supported
+preparation race, not proof of that historical interleaving.
+The [mirror setup record](evidence/SPN-128-mirror-setup-failure.json) retains both
+failed jobs. Neither printed its mirror file. Synthetic test profiles are not
+claimed to reproduce those exact missing contents; final CI must demonstrate
+the actual candidate's setup and workloads.
+
+Under [the runbook's verification-gap rule](../run-backlog.md#4-fix-here-or-file-separately)
+and the recorded [SPN-117 prerequisite](SPN-117.md), this PR may carry only the
+minimum proven preparation fixes needed to obtain its required acceptance:
+wait for the requested empty folder's loaded contents before disconnecting, and
+leave a non-Azure mirror profile unchanged by the Azure-specific optimization.
+The estimate is fewer than 100 changed executable lines, including extracting
+the existing mirror transform for focused tests, plus regression evidence and
+this decision record. Final actual counts belong in the PR.
+Neither fix changes application behavior, test assertions, timeouts, retries,
+runner selection or required gates. Strict validation remains before any Azure
+mirror rewrite; apt installation and its failures remain visible.
+
+Before changing folder readiness, the bounded sequence is three controlled
+fresh-profile held-folder probes, then three complete corrected first-attempt
+journeys, then one withheld-readiness negative case. No unchanged retries are
+authorized by this plan. The existing heading and New button may render from
+the shared list before the separate folder-detail response supplies the loaded
+view. The contents signal establishes synchronous view readiness; later offline
+reloads and publication assertions still prove persistence. If the probe instead
+finds an application persistence defect, reassess its ownership before expanding
+this slice. Preserve the original failure, diagnostic patches and each result.
+
+The [bounded readiness record](evidence/SPN-128-readiness.json) retains all
+seven attempts and the reproducible
+[held-folder](evidence/SPN-128-held-folder-probe.patch),
+[four-line repair](evidence/SPN-128-readiness-fix.patch) and
+[withheld-readiness](evidence/SPN-128-withheld-readiness.patch) patches.
+All three held-response probes reproduced heading/New visibility with loading
+still active, no contents and no prepared folder view; disconnecting then
+produced the missing view. All three complete corrected journeys passed their
+first attempts with the original content, access, reload, receipt and exactly-once
+publication assertions intact. The single negative case actually failed at the
+existing 5,000 ms Folder contents assertion before disconnecting or creating a
+document. Its exit 1 is negative-control evidence, not a passing journey.
+
+Each attempt used a fresh isolated browser context, fixture database and account,
+one worker and zero retries; it does not claim separate Chromium process restarts.
+Node 26.12.1, Playwright 1.64.1 and Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (revision 1248) were
+pinned. The serialized host-accounted watchdog reported 34.80 seconds/1,708.8 MiB
+for the three probes, 81.88 seconds/2,031.9 MiB for the three corrected journeys,
+and 45.17 seconds/1,692.1 MiB for the negative command, within its unchanged
+2 GiB/475-second bounds. Exact source, configuration, diagnostic and artifact
+hashes and the difference between assertion, suite and watchdog elapsed times
+are retained in the JSON. Only the four-line readiness repair runs in the
+committed fixture; diagnostic patches are evidence. These controlled results
+establish the preparation gap without claiming the historical timeout's exact
+interleaving or completing SPN-120's broader audit.
+
+Exercise mirror applicability with a non-Azure profile left byte-identical, the
+ordinary and already-preferred Azure pairs, and malformed Azure profiles that
+must still fail before writing. Record the actual runner-profile evidence and
+its limits rather than guessing its contents from the provider name.
+
+The [focused mirror checks](evidence/SPN-128-mirror-validation.json) passed all
+12 cases on pinned Node 26.12.1: synthetic profiles without the Azure hostname
+remain byte-identical, recognized priorities and surrounding bytes are preserved,
+and nine malformed Azure cases refuse. The serialized host-accounted watchdog
+reported 1.0 second and 105.3 MiB peak, within its 2 GiB/475-second bounds. The
+helper does not validate or rewrite profiles without that hostname; downstream
+apt and test steps still run normally. The original failed profiles remain
+unknown, and these local cases do not replace the actual final-head CI run.
+
+The prerequisite's actual executable diff is four added fixture lines, 39 added
+and 26 removed mirror-helper lines, and 48 new focused-test lines: 117 changed
+lines including tests. Most helper changes extract the existing strict transform
+for direct testing. This accounting excludes maintained evidence and prose;
+the final PR records the complete base-relative size.
+
+Operator receives required checks that reach their existing workloads and stop
+at an unfinished preparation phase. Owner and Collaborator retain the complete
+offline content, ownership, reload, access and exactly-once publication contract.
+Link guest gains no capability; its access and revocation checks stay required.
+This prerequisite claims no completion of SPN-120's historical fixture audit or
+broader cleanup work. Only SPN-128 is prepared for retirement by this PR; opening
+it does not authorize merging it.

-# 🌷 SPN-128 Reinstall the preserved original after an interrupted restore
-
-## Story
-
-As the [Owner](../product/personas.md#owner), I want a restore interrupted during its trial to reopen on the workspace's own preserved content, so that a power loss or timeout does not cost work saved after the last backup.
-
-## Scenarios
-
-### The host stops during the candidate's trial
-
-Given a confirmed restore that preserved the original and activated the candidate, then lost power or ran past its confirmation window before committing,
-When the supervisor restarts and the Operator follows the unresolved-restore runbook,
-Then a supported supervisor command verifies the preserved original against its frozen fingerprint and reinstalls it as a new generation,
-And the restore records **Original content was recovered**, with the recovered banner and the same access reconciliation as an in-flight rollback,
-And ambiguous or missing evidence still keeps the workspace closed.
-
-## Rules
-
-- Split by SPN-112's merge review, 2026-10-30: [disposition](../implementation/SPN-112.md#merge-review-dispositions). SPN-112 fails and reopens a restore that stopped before activation, stays fail-closed from activation onward, and documents fresh-host recovery from the last backup in `docs/maintenance.md`, which loses work after that backup.
-- The command is supervisor-owned and journaled with its own crash cuts, needs fresh Operator authority, and never copies raw files over a live or newly acknowledged generation. Reuse `reconcileRestoreRollback` and the original-recovery permit rather than a second rollback path.
-- Pre-launch: the launch drill (SPN-038) exercises restore on the target host, where an interruption today means lost work.
-- Persona weighing: the Owner and Collaborators keep their latest work; the Operator gets a supported exit instead of fresh-host recovery; Link guests are revoked either way.
-
-## Out of scope
-
-- Lifting the five-minute window (SPN-124); evidence pruning (SPN-125).
-
-## Verify
-
-- Real-process SIGKILL tests at trial-opening, activation, original-activation and original-commit, each followed by restart, the new command, and a check that the live fingerprint equals the frozen original's.
-- Runbook step in `docs/maintenance.md` replaced by the supported command.

+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import { preferUbuntuArchive } from './prefer-ubuntu-archive.ts';
+
+const azure = 'http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const archive = 'https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const security = 'https://security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const normal = `${azure}\tpriority:1\n${archive}\tpriority:2\n${security}\tpriority:3\n`;
+const preferred = `${azure}\tpriority:2\n${archive}\tpriority:1\n${security}\tpriority:3\n`;
+
+test('leaves profiles without Azure byte-identical', () => {
+  // Synthetic non-Azure inputs, not a claimed capture of a particular runner.
+  for (const original of [
+    '',
+    `${archive}\tpriority:1\n${security}\tpriority:2\n`,
+    '# runner-managed sources\r\nhttp://us-east-1.ec2.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/\tpriority:1\r\n',
+    'http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/\n',
+  ]) {
+    assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(original), original);
+  }
+});
+
+test('changes only the existing Azure/archive priorities and preserves other bytes', () => {
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(normal), preferred);
+  const original = `# mirrors\r\n  ${azure}\tpriority:1  \r\n\t${archive} priority:2\r\n${security}\tpriority:3\r\n`;
+  const expected = `# mirrors\r\n  ${azure}\tpriority:2  \r\n\t${archive} priority:1\r\n${security}\tpriority:3\r\n`;
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(original), expected);
+});
+
+test('keeps an already preferred Azure/archive pair unchanged', () => {
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(preferred), preferred);
+});
+
+for (const [name, original] of [
+  ['missing archive', `${azure}\tpriority:1\n`],
+  ['duplicate Azure', normal + `${azure}\tpriority:1\n`],
+  ['duplicate archive', normal + `${archive}\tpriority:2\n`],
+  ['equal priorities', normal.replace(`${archive}\tpriority:2`, `${archive}\tpriority:1`)],
+  ['unsupported priority', normal.replace(`${azure}\tpriority:1`, `${azure}\tpriority:3`)],
+  ['missing priority', normal.replace(`${azure}\tpriority:1`, azure)],
+  ['unexpected metadata', normal.replace('priority:1', 'priority:1 extra:yes')],
+  ['unrecognized Azure scheme', normal.replace(azure, azure.replace('http:', 'https:'))],
+  ['unrecognized Azure case', normal.replace('azure.archive', 'AZURE.archive')],
+]) {
+  test(`refuses malformed Azure profile: ${name}`, () => {
+    assert.throws(() => preferUbuntuArchive(original), /expected one Azure\/archive pair/);
+  });
+}

+# SPN-128 — recover a preserved original after interruption
+
+## Scope checkpoint
+
+2026-11-01, accepted for implementation by agent judgment under the standing
+persona delegation. The complete L outcome includes a supported cold-host
+command, separately journaled authority and crash cuts, immutable source proof,
+existing rollback reconciliation and original trial admission, terminal replay
+protection, real-process acceptance, and the maintained recovery runbook.
+SPN-124's operation lifetime and SPN-125's pruning remain separate.
+
+## Fresh cold-host authority and immutable restore history
+
+2026-11-01, accepted by agent judgment under the standing persona delegation.
+The question is how an Operator authorizes recovery when the interrupted
+restore's application proof has expired. Renewing that proof would change the
+meaning of the immutable intent; requiring a fresh application login would be
+impossible while the workspace is closed. The existing private host control
+socket supplies deliberate authority without either dependency.
+
+The existing private, service-UID-owned control socket is the Operator's
+cold-host authority when application sign-in is unavailable. A deliberate
+`recover-original --operation UUID` command obtains a new bounded grant for the
+exact unresolved job. It never refreshes the old passkey proof or rewrites its
+intent. The original phase/execution and each interrupted recovery attempt stay
+available as historical evidence. Missing or contradictory evidence keeps the
+workspace closed.
+
+Each grant uses the existing two-minute supervisor budget, with a hard ten-minute
+upper bound for configured test budgets. Each job retains at most eight cold
+attempts and still obeys the existing 64 KiB record bound; exhausted capacity
+refuses another attempt without deleting any evidence.
+These limits keep the command finite and the retained journal inspectable.
+Increasing operation lifetime and safely pruning retained evidence remain the
+separate SPN-124 and SPN-125 outcomes.
+
+Recovery uses the witnessed frozen original as the only content/access source
+and `reconcileRestoreRollback` for the existing access, receipt and generation
+reconciliation. Every known complete attempted image contributes negative
+evidence. A partially overwritten live database is retained as raw evidence and
+never opened as SQLite. An interrupted private trial must still match its sealed
+prepared fingerprint before its closed tuple can supply negative evidence.
+
+The existing `original` permit, private readiness and durable commitment protocol
+opens the result. A committed winner is immutable: retry/restart can finish
+opening that current generation but cannot reinstall old bytes over subsequent
+acknowledged work.
+
+A trial permit is journaled before the main journal adopts its child. A crash
+between those writes can leave a private process outside the main child field.
+Fresh host authority may stop only the exact selected planned group after
+checking the predecessor generation and operation authority, then the process
+boot, start time and ownership token. Recovery checks unchanged evidence and
+physical handle closure before granting a new attempt; other live groups still
+keep the workspace closed.
+
+Operator: a supported bounded command replaces manual fresh-host recovery.
+Owner and Collaborator: preserve work accepted after the most recent backup,
+including history, filing and access, with the established reconciliation fences.
+Link guest: old capability access is revoked as in ordinary original recovery.
+
+## What the fingerprint proves
+
+The frozen source's full logical fingerprint must match the independently
+persisted pre-shutdown witness. Reconciliation intentionally changes sessions,
+native generations, negative receipt evidence and the recovered notice. Therefore
+the final live fingerprint matches the newly prepared recovered output; original
+user content and access are checked separately. No fingerprint fields are
+excluded or weakened to force equality.
+
+## Verification
+
+The acceptance harness uses actual SIGKILL and restart at eleven historical
+restore cuts and six cold-command cuts. Fixture-only clocks expire the original
+proof and previous cold grants; this is clock-controlled expiry, not a wall-clock
+soak. Checks bind the source to its shutdown witness and the live result to the
+reconciled output before fresh authentication, verify revoked sessions and guest
+links, and preserve an acknowledged Owner edit and passkey counter across another
+restart and repeated command. Missing or altered originals and a changed private
+trial fingerprint must refuse without changing the live tuple or barrier.
+Exact executed source, check and review identities, measurements, and failure
+dispositions are maintained in [PR 229](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/229).
+Final CI and independent reviews must identify the same current committed source;
+this description of the harness does not claim those gates have already passed.
+
+## Required-validation prerequisites
+
+2026-11-01, accepted by agent judgment under the standing persona delegation.
+The first full acceptance run on `f3bdf95e1355de5bebf8ee64332b31201555b9c5`
+passed the 626-test recovery partition, including all 17 process crash cases,
+the 123 supervisor tests and both supervised-restore browser journeys. It also
+exposed two bounded preparation gaps in unchanged validation infrastructure:
+the Ubuntu mirror optimizer rejected an AWS runner profile before tests started,
+and the shared-folder offline-creation journey failed its first attempt before
+publication. Its automatic retry passed; `failOnFlakyTests` correctly kept the
+required gate failed. That retry is not evidence of repair.
+
+The maintained [browser first-attempt record](evidence/SPN-128-sync-production-first-attempt.json)
+retains the exact source, runtime, browser, original artifact digest, timeout,
+retry and observed state without credentials or document contents. Its seven-day
+raw CI artifact is supplementary and expires. The first attempt has no retained
+trace establishing its exact blocked action; its missing-folder screen and
+absence of forwarded creation are consistent with the source-supported
+preparation race, not proof of that historical interleaving.
+The [mirror setup record](evidence/SPN-128-mirror-setup-failure.json) retains both
+failed jobs. Neither printed its mirror file. Synthetic test profiles are not
+claimed to reproduce those exact missing contents; final CI must demonstrate
+the actual candidate's setup and workloads.
+
+Under [the runbook's verification-gap rule](../run-backlog.md#4-fix-here-or-file-separately)
+and the recorded [SPN-117 prerequisite](SPN-117.md), this PR may carry only the
+minimum proven preparation fixes needed to obtain its required acceptance:
+wait for the requested empty folder's loaded contents before disconnecting, and
+leave a non-Azure mirror profile unchanged by the Azure-specific optimization.
+The estimate is fewer than 100 changed executable lines, including extracting
+the existing mirror transform for focused tests, plus regression evidence and
+this decision record. Final actual counts belong in the PR.
+Neither fix changes application behavior, test assertions, timeouts, retries,
+runner selection or required gates. Strict validation remains before any Azure
+mirror rewrite; apt installation and its failures remain visible.
+
+Before changing folder readiness, the bounded sequence is three controlled
+fresh-profile held-folder probes, then three complete corrected first-attempt
+journeys, then one withheld-readiness negative case. No unchanged retries are
+authorized by this plan. The existing heading and New button may render from
+the shared list before the separate folder-detail response supplies the loaded
+view. The contents signal establishes synchronous view readiness; later offline
+reloads and publication assertions still prove persistence. If the probe instead
+finds an application persistence defect, reassess its ownership before expanding
+this slice. Preserve the original failure, diagnostic patches and each result.
+
+The [bounded readiness record](evidence/SPN-128-readiness.json) retains all
+seven attempts and the reproducible
+[held-folder](evidence/SPN-128-held-folder-probe.patch),
+[four-line repair](evidence/SPN-128-readiness-fix.patch) and
+[withheld-readiness](evidence/SPN-128-withheld-readiness.patch) patches.
+All three held-response probes reproduced heading/New visibility with loading
+still active, no contents and no prepared folder view; disconnecting then
+produced the missing view. All three complete corrected journeys passed their
+first attempts with the original content, access, reload, receipt and exactly-once
+publication assertions intact. The single negative case actually failed at the
+existing 5,000 ms Folder contents assertion before disconnecting or creating a
+document. Its exit 1 is negative-control evidence, not a passing journey.
+
+Each attempt used a fresh isolated browser context, fixture database and account,
+one worker and zero retries; it does not claim separate Chromium process restarts.
+Node 26.12.1, Playwright 1.64.1 and Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (revision 1248) were
+pinned. The serialized host-accounted watchdog reported 34.80 seconds/1,708.8 MiB
+for the three probes, 81.88 seconds/2,031.9 MiB for the three corrected journeys,
+and 45.17 seconds/1,692.1 MiB for the negative command, within its unchanged
+2 GiB/475-second bounds. Exact source, configuration, diagnostic and artifact
+hashes and the difference between assertion, suite and watchdog elapsed times
+are retained in the JSON. Only the four-line readiness repair runs in the
+committed fixture; diagnostic patches are evidence. These controlled results
+establish the preparation gap without claiming the historical timeout's exact
+interleaving or completing SPN-120's broader audit.
+
+Exercise mirror applicability with a non-Azure profile left byte-identical, the
+ordinary and already-preferred Azure pairs, and malformed Azure profiles that
+must still fail before writing. Record the actual runner-profile evidence and
+its limits rather than guessing its contents from the provider name.
+
+The [focused mirror checks](evidence/SPN-128-mirror-validation.json) passed all
+12 cases on pinned Node 26.12.1: synthetic profiles without the Azure hostname
+remain byte-identical, recognized priorities and surrounding bytes are preserved,
+and nine malformed Azure cases refuse. The serialized host-accounted watchdog
+reported 1.0 second and 105.3 MiB peak, within its 2 GiB/475-second bounds. The
+helper does not validate or rewrite profiles without that hostname; downstream
+apt and test steps still run normally. The original failed profiles remain
+unknown, and these local cases do not replace the actual final-head CI run.
+
+The prerequisite's actual executable diff is four added fixture lines, 39 added
+and 26 removed mirror-helper lines, and 48 new focused-test lines: 117 changed
+lines including tests. Most helper changes extract the existing strict transform
+for direct testing. This accounting excludes maintained evidence and prose;
+the final PR records the complete base-relative size.
+
+Operator receives required checks that reach their existing workloads and stop
+at an unfinished preparation phase. Owner and Collaborator retain the complete
+offline content, ownership, reload, access and exactly-once publication contract.
+Link guest gains no capability; its access and revocation checks stay required.
+This prerequisite claims no completion of SPN-120's historical fixture audit or
+broader cleanup work. Only SPN-128 is prepared for retirement by this PR; opening
+it does not authorize merging it.

-   confirmation's five-minute window](backups.md) after activation. The
-   preserved original is intact in the recovery root, but no supported command
-   reinstalls it yet ([SPN-128](todo/SPN-128.md)); copying those files back by hand
-   is not a recovery step. Copy the whole application directory and recovery root
-   read-only to separate encrypted storage, then follow
-   [fresh-host recovery](backups.md#restore-onto-a-fresh-host) from the last
-   verified backup with its access review. That loses work accepted after the
-   backup, so tell the Owner and Collaborators before reopening. Keep the copy
-   until that host is checked; it is the only evidence of the lost work.
+3. Run `status` again and read `lastFailure`. If it is `restore-job-pending`
+   or `original-recovery-unresolved`, continue at step 4. Otherwise follow
+   [First startup and restart](#first-startup-and-restart) to verify, start and
+   resume the selected live generation. Reuse `operationId` when status has one. Otherwise run
+   `node scripts/deploy/maintenance.ts verify` without an operation ID; it creates
+   one and returns the ID to use with start and resume. This also applies to a
+   committed backup or original in `recovery-required` after startup cleanup.
+   Sign in as the Operator and **Refresh restore status**. Only a recorded
+   outcome says which data is live.
+4. For `restore-job-pending` or `original-recovery-unresolved`, use the exact
+   `operationId` from status and run, as the deployment service UID. If status
+   provides no operation ID, keep the workspace closed and investigate under
+   step 5; do not invent an ID.
+
+   ```sh
+   node scripts/deploy/maintenance.ts recover-original --operation 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
+   ```
+
+   This deliberately authorizes recovery of the preserved original. The
+   supervisor verifies its independently recorded pre-shutdown fingerprint,
+   reconciles access and retry evidence exactly as an in-flight original
+   recovery, and installs a new generation through a private trial. It then
+   records **Original content was recovered** and reopens the workspace with
+   the recovered banner. Sign in again as the Operator and **Refresh restore
+   status**. Existing sessions and guest links are revoked; original accounts,
+   passkeys, content and grants are retained under the normal recovery rules.
+
+   Each command has a fixed time budget (two minutes in the standard supervisor)
+   and its own immutable grant and output slot. A failed or disconnected command
+   is not completion: inspect status and restart the supervisor before retrying
+   the same command/operation ID. Each retry retains earlier evidence and uses a
+   new grant; at most eight attempts are retained for this operation. If the
+   original already committed, the command only verifies/opens that selected
+   live generation. It never reinstalls prepared bytes over later acknowledged
+   work, and it refuses to replace a committed backup or a later generation.

+   policy, exhausted attempt capacity, or uncertain ownership keeps the workspace
+   closed. Do not copy raw files back by hand or delete the barrier. Preserve the
+   whole application directory and recovery root read-only on separate encrypted
+   storage and investigate that reported prerequisite. If the preserved original
+   cannot be proven, use [fresh-host recovery](backups.md#restore-onto-a-fresh-host)
+   from the last verified backup with its access review. That loses work accepted
+   after the backup; tell the Owner and Collaborators before reopening and retain
+   the evidence until recovery is checked. [SPN-128's decision](implementation/SPN-128.md)

-
-## Story
-
-As the [Owner](../product/personas.md#owner), I want a restore interrupted during its trial to reopen on the workspace's own preserved content, so that a power loss or timeout does not cost work saved after the last backup.
-
-## Scenarios
-
-### The host stops during the candidate's trial
-
-Given a confirmed restore that preserved the original and activated the candidate, then lost power or ran past its confirmation window before committing,
-When the supervisor restarts and the Operator follows the unresolved-restore runbook,
-Then a supported supervisor command verifies the preserved original against its frozen fingerprint and reinstalls it as a new generation,
-And the restore records **Original content was recovered**, with the recovered banner and the same access reconciliation as an in-flight rollback,
-And ambiguous or missing evidence still keeps the workspace closed.
-
-## Rules
-
-- Split by SPN-112's merge review, 2026-10-30: [disposition](../implementation/SPN-112.md#merge-review-dispositions). SPN-112 fails and reopens a restore that stopped before activation, stays fail-closed from activation onward, and documents fresh-host recovery from the last backup in `docs/maintenance.md`, which loses work after that backup.
-- The command is supervisor-owned and journaled with its own crash cuts, needs fresh Operator authority, and never copies raw files over a live or newly acknowledged generation. Reuse `reconcileRestoreRollback` and the original-recovery permit rather than a second rollback path.
-- Pre-launch: the launch drill (SPN-038) exercises restore on the target host, where an interruption today means lost work.
-- Persona weighing: the Owner and Collaborators keep their latest work; the Operator gets a supported exit instead of fresh-host recovery; Link guests are revoked either way.
-
-## Out of scope
-
-- Lifting the five-minute window (SPN-124); evidence pruning (SPN-125).
-
-## Verify
-
-- Real-process SIGKILL tests at trial-opening, activation, original-activation and original-commit, each followed by restart, the new command, and a check that the live fingerprint equals the frozen original's.
-- Runbook step in `docs/maintenance.md` replaced by the supported command.

+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import { preferUbuntuArchive } from './prefer-ubuntu-archive.ts';
+
+const azure = 'http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const archive = 'https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const security = 'https://security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/';
+const normal = `${azure}\tpriority:1\n${archive}\tpriority:2\n${security}\tpriority:3\n`;
+const preferred = `${azure}\tpriority:2\n${archive}\tpriority:1\n${security}\tpriority:3\n`;
+
+test('leaves profiles without Azure byte-identical', () => {
+  // Synthetic non-Azure inputs, not a claimed capture of a particular runner.
+  for (const original of [
+    '',
+    `${archive}\tpriority:1\n${security}\tpriority:2\n`,
+    '# runner-managed sources\r\nhttp://us-east-1.ec2.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/\tpriority:1\r\n',
+    'http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/\n',
+  ]) {
+    assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(original), original);
+  }
+});
+
+test('changes only the existing Azure/archive priorities and preserves other bytes', () => {
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(normal), preferred);
+  const original = `# mirrors\r\n  ${azure}\tpriority:1  \r\n\t${archive} priority:2\r\n${security}\tpriority:3\r\n`;
+  const expected = `# mirrors\r\n  ${azure}\tpriority:2  \r\n\t${archive} priority:1\r\n${security}\tpriority:3\r\n`;
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(original), expected);
+});
+
+test('keeps an already preferred Azure/archive pair unchanged', () => {
+  assert.equal(preferUbuntuArchive(preferred), preferred);
+});
+
+for (const [name, original] of [
+  ['missing archive', `${azure}\tpriority:1\n`],
+  ['duplicate Azure', normal + `${azure}\tpriority:1\n`],
+  ['duplicate archive', normal + `${archive}\tpriority:2\n`],
+  ['equal priorities', normal.replace(`${archive}\tpriority:2`, `${archive}\tpriority:1`)],
+  ['unsupported priority', normal.replace(`${azure}\tpriority:1`, `${azure}\tpriority:3`)],
+  ['missing priority', normal.replace(`${azure}\tpriority:1`, azure)],
+  ['unexpected metadata', normal.replace('priority:1', 'priority:1 extra:yes')],
+  ['unrecognized Azure scheme', normal.replace(azure, azure.replace('http:', 'https:'))],
+  ['unrecognized Azure case', normal.replace('azure.archive', 'AZURE.archive')],
+]) {
+  test(`refuses malformed Azure profile: ${name}`, () => {
+    assert.throws(() => preferUbuntuArchive(original), /expected one Azure\/archive pair/);
+  });
+}
